fatal_errors: The proposed HEBM-plus-SPS route, refractory BCC alloy family, and processing conditions do not reconstruct the target HPHT treatment of lamellar FCC/B2 Al0.7CoCrFeNi.

The cited evidence supports coherent nanoprecipitation as a design concept but does not establish that the proposed ball-milling and sub-recrystallization SPS schedule will produce coherent solute-rich precipitates or dynamic strain aging.

The mechanism inconsistently invokes Orowan bypass while also claiming facile dislocation transmission through coherent clusters; these correspond to different precipitate-dislocation interaction regimes.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad strength–ductility problem and proposes a testable alternative with useful tensile, EBSD, TEM, and APT measurements. Its coherent-interface stress-relief concept partially agrees with the target mechanism, and the experiment could determine whether clustering correlates with improved strain hardening. However, it changes the material from a eutectic FCC/B2 Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy to a refractory single-phase BCC system and replaces 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2 h HPHT processing with ball milling and short SPS. It therefore misses the target structural evolution, phase-to-phase dislocation transfer, specific deformation modes, fracture evolution, GND convergence, and approximately 1150 MPa/36% outcome. Evidence E1 supports coherent nanoprecipitates in tungsten refractory HEAs, while E5 supports their room-temperature brittleness, but none of the excerpts validates the proposed processing window, segregation kinetics, DSA mechanism, or quantitative gains. The baseline is also weakly framed: solution annealing commonly lowers defect density and may reduce strength rather than generically producing a high-strength state. A stronger discriminating design would add HEBM-only and SPS-only controls, density/porosity and contamination measurements, and a matched-temperature conventional treatment.
